newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS GET OFFENSE GOING IN ROUT OF SHARKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-CANUCKS GET OFFENSE GOING IN ROUT OF SHARKS.

text.p: The slumbering Vancouver Canucks offence came to life on Thursday with a 6-1 rout of the San Jose Sharks.

Alexander Mogilny had two goals and an assist and Martin Gelinas and Trevor Linden each added a goal and an assist for the Canucks, who won won for just the third time in their last nine games with the help of three powerplay goals.
Pavel Bure and Russ Courtnall also scored, while Vancouver goaltender Corey Hirsch, who had lost his last five decisions, turned aside 27 shots.

Hirsch carried a shutout into the third period before Tony Granato's fluke powerplay goal at 3:52 pulled San Jose within 4-1. Granato's centering pass hit Vancouver defenceman Adrian Aucoin's skate and deflected past Hirsch.
Bure restored the four-goal advantage by converting a breakaway with his 23rd goal of the season.
Vancouver's other Russian sniper Mogilny completed the scoring at 14:37 of the third with his second goal of the game and 26th of the season.

"It's a big lift, not only because we won, but six goals for us is pretty good, especially for a team that has had trouble scoring," said Hirsch, whose teammates victimised San Jose goalie Wade Flaherty six times on 29 shots.
At Florida, defenceman Ken Daneyko scored just his second goal of the season at 7:11 of the third period to lift the New Jersey Devils into a 2-2 tie with the Panthers.
With their third tie in five days the Devils stretched their club-record unbeaten streak to 13 games (6-0-7).
New Jersey goaltender Martin Brodeur made 25 saves to extend his personal unbeaten streak to 14 games.
Mark Fitzpatrick made 24 saves for the Panthers, who got goals from Rob Niedermayer and Bill Lindsay. Pascal Rheaume, playing his first NHL game, scored the other New Jersey goal.
At Tampa Bay, Chris Gratton and Daymond Langkow each had a goal and an assist and Rick Tabaracci stopped 28 shots to lead the Lightning to a 5-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers.
Bill Houlder and Shawn Burr added two assists apiece for the Lightning.
Eric Lindros and Rod Brind'Amour scored for Philadelphia as the teams combined for five goals in a wild first period.
Gratton beat Ron Hextall at 5:22 of the opening period to snap a 1-1 tie and cap a spree of three goals in 65 seconds.
Dino Ciccarelli, Roman Hamrlik and Jason Wiemer also scored for Tampa Bay.

In Chicago, Jeff Shantz set up two goals, including a pivotal tally by Brent Sutter late in the third period, and Tony Amonte notched his 32nd goal help the Blackhawks to a 5-3 win over the Boston Bruins.

Chicago jumped out to 3-0 lead, but the Bruins twice closed to within one -- on a short-handed goal by Sheldon Kennedy that made it 3-2 and a powerplay tally by Rick Tocchet that took the score to 4-3.
Sutter sealed the win by scoring with 1:46 remaining as five different Blackhawks put the puck past Bill Ranford.
Jeff Hackett made 34 stops for Chicago.
In St Louis, Radek Bonk scored off a rebound 9:41 into the third period to lift the Ottawa Senators into a 1-1 tie with the Blues.
St Louis goaltender Grant Fuhr held the Senators off the scoreboard over the first two periods before Bonk knotted the score. Fuhr finished with 26 saves.

Jim Campbell was the only one to beat Ottawa goalie Damian Rhodes when he scored his 21st goal with 7:59 left in the second period. Rhodes made 25 saves, including a key stop of a Brett Hull slap shot in overtime.
In Los Angeles, Jeff Shevalier scored twice
